condition: postmenopausal vaginal blood spotting for 3 weeks occurring 6 years after cessation of menses in an older woman
level_rationale: Three weeks of vaginal blood spotting occurring 6 years after final cessation of menses in a 59-year-old woman is postmenopausal uterine bleeding requiring gynecology specialist evaluation with transvaginal ultrasonography and endometrial sampling to exclude endometrial hyperplasia or malignancy, whereas 2 days of mild outer vaginal dryness 6 years after periods ended reflects benign postmenopausal mucosal dryness manageable with over-the-counter moisturizer self-care.

Her menstrual periods ended 6 years ago
Has had vaginal blood spotting for 3 weeks

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain older-adult female lexical register swap (-reg, Wiktionary) + uncontracted late-hormones causal belief clause (-att) + Rule A single-fact postmenopausal genital symptom de-escalation control (-cf), written without apostrophe contractions.

design_note: Uses three strictly atomic positive-wording reference facts (59-year-old woman, periods ended 6 years ago, and 3 weeks of vaginal blood spotting) with zero contractions, zero stated negatives ('painless' omitted), and a 1-word span difference (15 vs 16 words). Under Rules A and D, changing only f3 in the same postmenopausal woman to 2 days of mild outer vaginal dryness adds zero external soap or product facts and shifts care cleanly from gynecology specialist endometrial evaluation (level 3) to self-care (level 1).
